Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine
- Published
Russia was behind an arson attack on an Estonian defence company in the capital Tallinn last month, authorities say.
Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the attack on Milrem Robotics - which supplies Ukraine with unmanned military vehicles - was ordered by Russian special services, but gave no details.
Moscow has been accused of launching sabotage attacks in a number of Nato countries that have been helping Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022.
Russia denies such allegations and has been quick to reject the Estonian accusation, too. But EU countries have rushed to Estonia's support, adding such attacks will not deter them from helping Ukraine.
The attack on Milrem Robotics occurred on the night of 14-15 August.
Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said that, based on information collected by the country's Internal Security Service, "we can conclude with certainty that the arson attack... was an act of sabotage ordered by the special services of the Russian Federation".
Security service chief Margo Palloson told broadcaster ERR that Russia was "constantly planning, looking for opportunities, trying to find people who would carry out attacks", but that last month's arson attack was its first successful attack this year.
The foreign minister said the perpetrators had been arrested and Palloson said they were Latvians who had been living in Russia and taken part in previous attacks. Three suspects were arrested in Latvia and extradited to Estonia earlier this month.
Margus Tsahkna said that "this act of sabotage is part of Russia's broader campaign across Europe, aimed at intimidating us and weakening our support for Ukraine".
French President Emmanuel Macron responded to Estonia's assessment, saying "the multiplication of these hostile acts represents a dangerous escalation by Russia, which will only lead it into a dead end".
He mentioned the incident at Leipzig airport in Germany in August, in which an explosive-laden drone was found near Ukrainian cargo planes.
"Russia needs to know that it will not overcome our unity or our determination to continue supporting Ukraine," Macron added.
An EU spokesman said the 27-member bloc would not cease supporting Ukraine.
Nato chief Mark Rutte urged European governments to stay calm and continue supporting Ukraine.

corpus.title: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence factory that produces vehicles Ukraine has used
corpus.signal_text:
Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence factory that produces vehicles Ukraine has used
3 Latvian citizens were arrested for mid-August crime and extradited to Estonia
Estonian authorities said Tuesday they have concluded that an arson attack in mid-August on a defence company that provides military vehicles to Ukraine was an act of sabotage commissioned by Russian security services.
Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said that "such actions are absolutely unacceptable" and that Russia's charge d'affaires in Tallinn was being summoned to his ministry.
A fire broke out overnight on Aug. 15 at a building in the Estonian capital used by Milrem Robotics, but was quickly brought under control, the BNS news agency reported. On Aug. 17, two Latvian suspects were detained in neighbouring Latvia, and a third followed the next day.
The suspects were handed over to Estonia.
Milrem has supplied THeMIS unmanned ground vehicles to Ukraine.
The Estonian Internal Security Service said that it has concluded that the arson attack "was a deliberate and pre-planned act commissioned by Russian security services."
It said in a statement that "the modus operandi of the Milrem attack is consistent with other acts of sabotage carried out in Europe on behalf of Russia," adding that it "assesses that the attack is directly attributable to the Russian Federation."
Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal wrote on X that "we will not be intimidated."
Russia scoffs at accusation
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said that "such statements are unfounded, ill-considered, absolutely not reflecting the reality, not containing any substantiation whatsoever."
"We cannot take such statements seriously, and we won't," Peskov said.
Moscow has been widely accused by Western officials of running a campaign of sabotage and disruption with the aim of undermining support for Ukraine and destabilizing European nations.
The Associated Press has tracked around 200 incidents of sabotage and malign activity across Europe blamed on Russia since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022.
That includes organizing plots to set fire to warehouses, launching drones and trying to kill enemies abroad as well as stealing defense technology and carrying out cyberattacks on critical European infrastructure.
In a recent case that pointed to an escalation of such activity, Germany blamed Russia for an attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport in early August using a drone laden with explosives.

NATO, EU allies rally to Estonia after ‘sabotage’ blamed on Russia
Tallinn – EU and NATO leaders on Tuesday rallied in support of Estonia and Ukraine after Tallinn accused Russia of “sabotage” in an August arson attack on a drone manufacturer, a claim the Kremlin immediately rejected.
“Russia continues its reckless campaign of hostile actions against NATO allies. It is trying to weaken our resolve and stop our support for Ukraine,” NATO chief Mark Rutte said.
He added: “But Russia is failing. It is failing on the battlefield in Ukraine and it is failing to undermine our unity and support for Ukraine.”
Estonia’s foreign minister, Margus Tsahkna, said an investigation into the August 15 arson attack against the defence company Milrem Robotics, which makes ground drones used in Ukraine, determined that Moscow was responsible.
“We can conclude with certainty that the arson attack… was an act of sabotage ordered by the special services of the Russian Federation,” he said on X.
He said the perpetrators had been arrested, and Russia’s ambassador had been summoned.
Tsahkna said that “this act of sabotage is part of Russia’s broader campaign across Europe, aimed at intimidating us and weakening our support for Ukraine”.
– Kremlin denial –
The Kremlin swiftly dismissed Estonia’s accusation as “baseless” and with “absolutely no relation to reality”.
“We cannot and will not take such statements seriously,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters in Moscow in response to an AFP question.
Estonia has repeatedly accused Russia of hybrid provocations since the beginning of Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Along with its neighbours, Latvia and Lithuania, the country has ramped up defence investment and remains a staunch ally of Kyiv.
The European Union said it stood with Estonia calling the arson attack “reckless”, and would not be put off supporting Ukraine.
“Moscow is trying to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine. This will not happen,” European Commission spokesman Christian Wigand said.

“Russia needs to know that it will not overcome our unity or our determination to continue supporting Ukraine,” Macron said on X.

NATO-Ostflanke Estland macht Russland für Brandanschlag verantwortlich
Estland wirft Russland Sabotage vor: Hinter einem Brandanschlag auf eine Rüstungsfirma in Tallinn steckt nach neuesten Erkenntnisse Russland. NATO-Chef Rutte rief die Bündnismitglieder auf, ruhig zu bleiben.
Es war Mitte August - am Gebäude eines Herstellers von Militärsystemen im estnischen Tallinn brach ein Feuer aus, das schnell unter Kontrolle gebracht werden konnte. Die Behörden leiteten Ermittlungen ein, die nun zu dem Schluss kommen: Russland steckt dahinter. Dies teilte Regierungschef Kristen Michal unter Berufung auf Ermittlungsergebnisse der Sicherheitsbehörden mit. Das estnische Außenministerium bestellte den Geschäftsträger der russischen Botschaft ein. Der baltische EU- und NATO-Staat hat eine Grenze zu Russland.
"Wir können heute mit Gewissheit sagen, dass der Brandanschlag auf das Rüstungsunternehmen Milrem Robotics in der Nacht vom 14. auf den 15. August ein Sabotageakt war, der von den russischen Geheimdiensten angeordnet wurde", sagte Michal. Der estnische Inlandsgeheimdienst sei nach eingehender Auswertung der gesammelten Informationen zu diesem Schluss gekommen. Die mutmaßlichen Täter seien festgenommen worden.
"Solche Aktivitäten sind absolut inakzeptabel und unverantwortlich", sagte Michal. Zugleich verdeutlichen sie nach seiner Einschätzung Moskaus wachsende Verzweiflung in einer Situation, in der Russland die Ziele seiner Aggression gegen die Ukraine nicht erreichen könne.
Russland weist Anschuldigungen zurück
Russland wies die estnischen Vorwürfe zurück. Die Anschuldigungen seien unbegründet, unüberlegt und nicht ernst zu nehmen, sagte Kremlsprecher Dmitri Peskow der russischen Staatsagentur Tass zufolge.
Der estnische Sicherheitspolizei-Chef Margo Palloson sagte, dass Russland ständig derartige Aktivitäten plane und nach Gelegenheiten und Personen suche, die die Taten verüben könnten. "Wir haben die überwiegende Mehrheit der Angriffe verhindert", sagte er dem estnischen Rundfunk, ohne nähere Angaben zu machen. Palloson betonte, dass Estland ein sicheres Land sei.
